claims.claim_ar: آتَيْنَا فعل ماضٍ بصيغة المتكلم الجمع (فَعَلْنَا) من الفعل آتَى/أَتَى، بمعنى «أَعْطَيْنَا/وَهَبْنَا». الحرف الواو هنا حرف عطف.
claims.claim_en: The verb 'آتَيْنَا' is the perfect (past) 1st-person plural (we- form) of the verb آتَى/أَتَى, meaning 'we gave/granted'. The initial وَ is the conjunction 'and'.
claims.needs_review_reason: The precise classification of آتَى (relation to أتى/آتى and any Form‑IV labeling) and orthography of the root (أ-ت-ى vs. ا-ت-ي) should be cross-checked with a lexicon.

claims.claim_ar: الاسم «دَاوُود» على وزن فَعُول (اسم علم)، مشتق تقليدياً من جذر د-و-د.
claims.claim_en: The name 'Dawud' (David) follows the noun pattern fa'ūl (فَعُول) and is conventionally derived from the root d-w-d.
claims.needs_review_reason: Proper-name morphological analysis can vary; verify root-letter assignment and semantic nuance in classical lexica.

claims.claim_ar: «زَبُور» اسم لكتاب مزمور/زبور (الصحف المزمورية)، مشتق عن الجذر ز-ب-ر
claims.claim_en: Zabur is a noun denoting the (Psalms) scripture; it is derived from the root z-b-r and functions as the name of that revealed book.
